message.content:
The area of the square is \(49\), so its side length is

\[
\sqrt{49}=7.
\]

Folding one pair of opposite corners together makes the crease the other diagonal of the square. Unfolding gives two congruent right isosceles triangles, each having legs of length \(7\).

For one triangle, the hypotenuse is the square’s diagonal:

\[
7\sqrt{2}.
\]

So the perimeter of one triangle is

\[
7+7+7\sqrt{2}=14+7\sqrt{2}.
\]

The answer is \(14+7\sqrt{2}\).
